facts.statement: Volgadraco, meaning "Volga River dragon", is a genus of pterosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of European Russia.
facts.quote: Volgadraco ("Volga River dragon") is a genus of pterosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of European Russia.

facts.statement: Volgadraco was described in 2008 by Averianov, Arkhangelsky, and Pervushov.
facts.quote: Volgadraco was described in 2008 by Averianov, Arkhangelsky, and Pervushov.

facts.statement: The type species is V. bogolubovi, with the specific name honoring Russian paleontologist Nikolai Nikolaevich Bogolubov.
facts.quote: The type species is V. bogolubovi, the specific name honouring Russian paleontologist Nikolai Nikolaevich Bogolubov.

facts.statement: Volgadraco lived during the early Campanian, a time between older Santonian or Turonian azhdarchids and later Maastrichtian azhdarchids.
facts.quote: The size of this animal, and the development of blood supply in the lower jaw are intermediate between older Santonian or Turonian azhdarchids like Azhdarcho and Bakonydraco and later Maastrichtian azhdarchids like Quetzalcoatlus.

facts.statement: In 2020, Averianov and Arkhangelsky classified Volgadraco as a member of the family Pteranodontidae.
facts.quote: In 2020, Averianov and Arkhangelsky reconsidered both Bogolubovia and Volgadraco as members of the family Pteranodontidae.

facts.statement: In 2026, Averianov and Arkhangelsky debated the validity of the genus, suggesting its fossils might belong to different types of pterosaurs.
facts.quote: In 2026, Averianov and Arkhangelsky regarded the hypodigm of Volgadraco as comprising fossils of different types of pterosaurs.

facts.statement: The Spanish taxobox lists Volgadraco as belonging to the family Azhdarchidae.
Volgadraco lived from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
